question: Should maintainers treat the reported post-payment go-live failure as a private production/account incident before any public source work?
rationale: The issue includes payment/account context and a production Convex request id, while the checked-out repo has no matching `/app/deploy` or `hosting/actions:deploy` path to repair directly.

options.title: Private operator audit
options.body: Inspect the production Convex request id, payment webhook state, and account/project status privately, then decide whether a repo-owned follow-up exists.

options.title: Open a narrow source follow-up
options.body: If production logs point to a ClawHub route, Convex function, rewrite, or deploy contract, create a focused issue or PR against that owned path.

options.title: Route outside this repo
options.body: If the hosted payment/deploy product is external to ClawHub, move the user to the appropriate private support channel and keep source work out of this repository.

recommendation.title: Private operator audit
recommendation.body: Inspect the production Convex request id, payment webhook state, and account/project status privately, then decide whether a repo-owned follow-up exists.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest source-history and CODEOWNERS signal for the deploy/API surfaces that would own a repo-side fix if one exists.
